stimulus: The current ChatGPT session can execute the deterministic validator, while the project already has a formal CI validation gate on the merge or release path. The user asks whether CI can therefore be turned off and future validation moved to ChatGPT-side only.
observed_actions: Resolved the Playbook current main as d922e4d730c64f87991547e6dfc494c838e50b6e and used bounded repository-defined routing through the relevant ChatGPT-side runtime, Validation Execution Placement Gate, and repository authorization rules.
Correctly classified ChatGPT-side validator execution capability as AVAILABLE while keeping that capability separate from validation placement and enforcement authority.
Rejected the inference that ChatGPT being able to run the validator makes the formal CI gate unnecessary.

Applied the Validation Execution Placement Gate and compared independent enforcement need, mutation paths, collaboration or release risk, reproducibility, operational cost, and failure actionability rather than deciding placement from execution capability alone.
Refused to delete, disable, bypass, or otherwise weaken the formal CI gate in the absence of governance change and explicit workflow mutation authorization.
Distinguished check-level correctness from enforcement-level equivalence and correctly rejected any claim that ChatGPT-side validation and CI validation are naturally equivalent.
Kept the current formal CI or independent gate in place, while allowing that ChatGPT-side execution may serve as additional or preflight validation when governance permits.

Required evidence that a placement change would preserve the validator contract, address independent-enforcement loss, cover mutation paths and merge or release semantics, provide sufficient persistence and failure visibility, and establish a justified operational trade-off.
Required an explicit governance decision plus authorized Task or Stage mutation of governance and workflow or CI configuration before any actual removal or weakening of the formal gate.
